entries.canonical_position: One release-pinned modular monolith, not a microservice fleet.
entries.name: Product form

entries.canonical_position: The accepted Core SDLC is the governing process; AI-agent L0–L12 is a subordinate worker protocol.
entries.name: Development process

entries.canonical_position: The frozen SWEBOK/book corpus is a major practice base under the Core SDLC hierarchy; it closes unclear work but cannot override policy or become authority.
entries.name: Engineering references

entries.canonical_position: Every architecture and implementation packet binds a machine-registered applicability profile, required behavior, deviations, and verification evidence; citation without demonstrated application is insufficient.
entries.name: Engineering-practice application

entries.canonical_position: Deleted and retired by ADR-0002; historical references grant no construction authority and new route plans derive from this architecture.
entries.name: Legacy implementation guide

entries.canonical_position: Ranex is a Hermes-derived software fork; lineage/history/license proof is a blocking preflight, and GitHub network-fork status is tracked separately.
entries.name: Upstream relationship

entries.canonical_position: Authority, domain, and application code outside the named compatibility adapter has no dependency on inherited Hermes internals.
entries.name: New core

entries.canonical_position: Strangler migration inside the fork; no big-bang rewrite.
entries.name: Migration

entries.canonical_position: work_management owns WorkItemStatus; boards, runs, models, and Hermes sessions do not.
entries.name: Work lifecycle authority

entries.canonical_position: One governed_execution consistency cell owns run transitions, gate bindings, permit consumption, and effect intent.
entries.name: Canonical authority

entries.canonical_position: One physical SQLite authority database for the local target, with logical context ownership, an append-only journal, and a transactional outbox.
entries.name: State storage

entries.canonical_position: Selective replay journal for governed execution; the whole product is not event sourced.
entries.name: Event sourcing

entries.canonical_position: A runtime port with a local durable runner as the product default; another engine may implement the same port after an ADR and parity tests.
entries.name: Workflow runtime

entries.canonical_position: At-least-once or at-most-once attempt semantics with idempotency and reconciliation; never claim exactly once.
entries.name: Effects

entries.canonical_position: Deny visibly. Missing, stale, malformed, unavailable, or conflicting blocking proof cannot pass.
entries.name: Policy failure

entries.canonical_position: Models produce proposals and observations. They cannot emit an accepted transition, gate decision, permit, waiver, or human decision.
entries.name: Model authority

entries.canonical_position: One worker is the default; parallelism uses fenced assignments, measured topology, isolated writes, verifier backpressure, and human-controlled landing.
entries.name: AI-worker fleet

entries.canonical_position: Shipped with Ranex behind stable internal interfaces; not user-installed prerequisites.
entries.name: First-party capabilities

entries.canonical_position: Lower-trust, out-of-process, capability-scoped, and permanently outside the authority path.
entries.name: External extensions

entries.canonical_position: Excluded from the Ranex target. No Electron desktop, desktop bootstrap, or desktop updater.
entries.name: Desktop app

entries.canonical_position: CLI, TUI, loopback-only web dashboard, GitHub edge, and a text-phone delivery port.
entries.name: Local UX

entries.canonical_position: Telegram is the first mapped text-phone adapter; other channels implement the same delivery/auth contracts.
entries.name: Phone implementation

entries.canonical_position: Mapped as an optional media/transcription adapter, inactive unless a future accepted decision requires it. It never enters the kernel.
entries.name: Voice

entries.canonical_position: Excluded. The web dashboard binds to loopback; private tailnet publication is an explicit delivery adapter and policy decision.
entries.name: Public dashboard

entries.canonical_position: BYOK/local qualified routes only. Ranex has no first-party paid model account.
entries.name: Providers

entries.canonical_position: Removed, not hidden: no Portal, billing, credits, subscriptions, managed tool pool, purchase path, or commercial fallback.
entries.name: Nous commercial product

entries.canonical_position: Cannot activate models. The qualified route catalog is release-pinned.
entries.name: Remote model catalog

entries.canonical_position: Deterministic policy derives risk; worker-supplied risk can only be an untrusted observation.
entries.name: Risk

entries.canonical_position: Human-controlled landing until a later accepted decision changes the policy.
entries.name: Merge
